article.title: Six Cocktails Worth Learning Properly
article.body:
Six Cocktails Worth Learning Properly

Learn six classics and you can make almost any cocktail: the Daiquiri and Margarita (sours), the Old Fashioned, Martini and Negroni (spirit-forward drinks), and the Tom Collins (a highball). Drinks House 247 recommends measuring every ingredient with a jigger, using plenty of fresh ice, and squeezing citrus juice fresh on the day.

Most cocktails are variations on a handful of templates. Master one sour, a couple of stirred spirit-forward drinks and a highball, and you understand the logic behind hundreds of others. If you are hosting this weekend, these six cover every taste at the table.

What do you need?

  • A jigger for measuring. Guessing is the main reason home cocktails taste unbalanced.
  • A shaker for drinks with citrus, and a mixing glass and bar spoon for drinks without.
  • A strainer.
  • Plenty of ice, fresh from the freezer, plus one large cube or block for the Old Fashioned and Negroni.
  • Fresh lemons and limes. Bottled juice tastes flat.
  • Simple syrup: equal parts sugar and hot water, stirred until dissolved and cooled. It keeps for a few weeks in the fridge.

The six specs

Cocktail Template Recipe Method Glass
DaiquiriSour50ml white rum, 25ml lime juice, 15ml simple syrupShake hard, double strainChilled coupe
MargaritaSour50ml blanco tequila, 25ml orange liqueur, 25ml lime juiceShake hard, strain over fresh iceRocks glass, half salted rim
Old FashionedSpirit-forward50ml bourbon or rye, 5 to 10ml simple syrup, 2 dashes Angostura bittersStir over ice, serve on one large cubeRocks glass, orange twist
MartiniSpirit-forward60ml gin or vodka, 10 to 15ml dry vermouthStir until very cold, strainChilled coupe or Martini glass, lemon twist or olive
NegroniSpirit-forward25ml gin, 25ml sweet vermouth, 25ml CampariStir over ice, serve on one large cubeRocks glass, orange slice or twist
Tom CollinsHighball50ml gin, 25ml lemon juice, 15ml simple syrup, topped with about 100ml sodaShake the first three, strain over ice, top with sodaTall glass, lemon wheel

The technique that matters for each

Daiquiri: the shake

The classic Daiquiri is nothing like the frozen slush. It is three ingredients in balance, so the shake does the work: fill the shaker with ice and shake hard for 10 to 12 seconds until the tin is frosted. That chills, dilutes and aerates the drink. Double strain through a fine sieve to remove ice shards.

Margarita: the balance

Limes vary, so taste. If the drink is too sharp, add a few millilitres of simple syrup; too sweet, a little more lime. Salt only half the rim so each sip can be taken with or without it.

Old Fashioned: the ice

A large, clear cube melts slowly, so the drink stays cold without becoming watery. Stir the ingredients with ice in a mixing glass first, then strain over the big cube. Express the oil from a strip of orange peel over the top by twisting it, skin side down.

Martini: the cold

Stir, do not shake, for about 30 seconds, until the outside of the mixing glass is ice cold. Shaking clouds the drink and adds ice chips. Keep your vermouth in the fridge and replace it within a month or two of opening; stale vermouth is the most common reason a home Martini tastes wrong.

Negroni: the proportions

Equal parts make it easy to remember, and easy to adjust. If it is too bitter for your taste, reduce the Campari slightly. Stir briefly over ice and serve over a large cube with an orange garnish.

Tom Collins: the bubbles

Shake the gin, lemon and syrup, strain into a tall glass full of ice, then top with cold soda and stir once, gently. Adding the soda last keeps the drink lively. The same template works with vodka, whisky or tequila.

Once you know these, you know dozens more

  • Swap the Daiquiri's rum for gin and lemon and you have a Gin Sour; add egg white for a silkier texture.
  • Swap the Margarita's tequila for brandy and you are close to a Sidecar.
  • Swap the Old Fashioned's spirit for aged rum, cognac or añejo tequila.
  • Swap the Negroni's gin for bourbon and you have a Boulevardier.
  • Swap the Martini's dry vermouth for sweet, and the gin for rye, and you are near a Manhattan.

Hosting tips

Batch stirred drinks such as Negronis ahead of time: mix the spirits in a bottle, add about 20% water for dilution, and chill in the fridge so they can be poured straight over ice. Shaken drinks are best made to order. Offer an alcohol-free option and plenty of water, and use measured pours so guests can keep track of what they are drinking.

Frequently asked questions

What are the six basic cocktails everyone should know?

The Daiquiri, Margarita, Old Fashioned, Martini, Negroni and Tom Collins. Together they cover the main templates: sours, spirit-forward drinks and highballs.

Should a Martini be shaken or stirred?

Stirred. Stirring chills and dilutes the drink while keeping it clear and silky. Shaking clouds it and adds ice chips.

What is the recipe for a Negroni?

Equal parts gin, sweet vermouth and Campari, 25ml of each, stirred over ice and served on a large cube with an orange garnish.

Why do cocktails at home taste different from bars?

Usually because of measuring, ice and freshness. Use a jigger, plenty of fresh ice and freshly squeezed citrus, and keep vermouth in the fridge.

Stocking the bar

Browse gin, rum, blanco tequila, bourbon and mixers, or read our home bar guide. For more, see our Negroni guide, why ice matters in cocktails and how to stock a drinks trolley.

Deliveries are to over-18s only under our Challenge 25 policy. Please drink responsibly.
